title: The written p^10 guards still cover the column-gap 2-norm ceiling (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/gaussian-twonorm-guard/`. It answers open question 2 of #4402: do any #4100 precision guards change when the inverse 2-norm drops from the bandwidth form to `1/sqrt(delta delta_col)`?

**Claim type:** a caller inventory plus an exact comparison under the floors already written in `GAUSSIAN.md`. **No new κ.** This does not prove a column gap for the rounded reference `H`.

- The callers in `research/unconditional-batched-crt` write exponents 10, 20, 40, 42, 45, 48, 100, 128 and 400. `AUDIT.md` names the notes and writes no `p^10`. The broad `< p^6` sentence does not use the bandwidth formula.
- For every integer `p >= 2`, with bandwidth `b <= p - 1` and `delta >= 1/(16p^2)`, the bandwidth 2-norm ceiling is strictly below `p^10`. At `p = 2` it is not below `p^9`, so 10 is the smallest uniform exponent for that corner.
- If `delta_col` meets the same floor, the column-gap ceiling is at most `16p^2`, also strictly below `p^10`.
- Both ceilings satisfy the hypothesis those later exponents assume, so none of them has to increase. At `p = 19` the bandwidth ceiling is already below `p^6` and the column-gap ceiling is below `p^3`.

## Test plan

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-twonorm-guard
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/gaussian-twonorm-guard outcome=completed
```

Maintainer replay has not been run. Head: `25cf6de154c641faaf6c85fe6e9bf5f51bdeb57e`. Base: canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`, priority revision 7, selected record unchanged. Checked 2026-10-21T16:40:11Z.

## Not covered

- Cross-cut entries, truncation and rounding, so `delta_col >= 1/(16p^2)` is not claimed for `H`.
- A smaller halo or normalizer. That arithmetic is the open next question; it is not required for correctness.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19102318
